Rashi on Chullin 22a:10:1.hebrew: כל מקום שנאמר אצבע וכהונה - ומוקמינן בפ"ק דמנחות (דף י.): או אצבע או כהונה, וגמר ממצורע עני דכתיב ביה "וטבל הכהן אצבעו הימנית", ומיניה ילפינן לכל היכא דכתיב כהן או אצבע שתהא עבודה בימין. ובעולת נדבה כתיב "כהן", "והקריב הכהן":
Rashi on Chullin 22a:10:1.english: Anywhere that "finger" and "priesthood" are stated - And we establish in the first chapter of Menachot (page 10a) [that this means] either "finger" or "priesthood" [alone suffices]. And [the Gemara] derives it from the poor metzora, regarding whom it is written, "And the priest shall dip his right finger," and from it we learn that anywhere that "priest" or "finger" is written, the service must be done with the right hand. And regarding a voluntary burnt offering, "priest" is written: "And the priest shall offer it."

Rashi on Chullin 22a:11:1.hebrew: ואידך - הא דאוקמינן במנחות "או אצבע או כהונה", הני מילי לרבנן; אבל לרבי שמעון אוקימנא התם דכהונה בעיא אצבע, דאע"ג דכתיב כהונה, אי לא כתיב בה אצבע לא גמרינן בה ימין. ות"ק דלעיל כר"ש סבירא ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:11:1.english: And the other - That which we established in Menachot, "either a finger or priesthood," this applies only according to the Rabbis. But according to Rabbi Shimon, we established there that priesthood requires a finger: even though "priesthood" is written, if "finger" were not written with it, we would not derive from it [the requirement of] the right hand. And the Tanna Kamma above holds like Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:12:1.english: And the first Tanna - who said "in accordance with the law of an animal sin-offering."

Rashi on Chullin 22a:12:2.hebrew: ור"א בר"ש - דאמר "כמשפט חטאת העוף", ומפיק היקישא לאחיזת ראש וגוף:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:12:2.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon - Who says "like the ordinance of the sin-offering of the bird," and derives the analogy [as applying] to holding the head and the body.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:12:3.hebrew: מול עורף - בעולה מנא להו תרתי, לא מצי גמרינן מיניה. דאי מצטרכא לן היקישא למול עורף, תו לא ילפת מיניה אחיזת ראש וגוף, דחילוקא דוהקריבו לגמרי ממעט להבדלה בעולה מדין חטאת. דהכי משמע: חלק הכתוב בעולה ממליקת חטאת, והטעינה הבדלה, וכל שישנו בשחיטה ישנו בהבדלה:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:12:3.english: Opposite the nape - In the case of an olah, how do they [the Rabbis] know both things? They cannot derive them from it [the verse]. For if we need the comparison [of olah to chatat] for [the requirement of melikah] opposite the nape, you could no longer derive from it [the requirement of] holding the head and the body, since the distinction of "and he shall bring it near" entirely excludes an olah from the law of a chatat with respect to separation [of the head from the body]. For this is what it means: The verse distinguished the olah from the melikah of a chatat, and imposed separation upon it, and whatever is subject to shechita is subject to separation.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:12:4.hebrew: גמרי מליקה ממליקה - במה מצינו? מה מליקה האמורה בחטאת פירש לך בה הכתוב "מול עורף", אף כל מליקה אינה אלא ממול עורף:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:12:4.english: They derive melika from melika - In what way did we find [this]? Just as with the melika stated regarding the sin-offering, Scripture specified for you "opposite the nape" (Leviticus 5:8), so too every melika is only from opposite the nape.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:13:1.english: With turtledoves - [This is] the language of the mishna:

Rashi on Chullin 22a:13:2.hebrew: ה"ג במתניתין תחלת הציהוב שבזה ושבזה פסול - תחלת הציהוב, כשמתחילין להביא נוצה יפה צהובה סביב לצואר, פסולין בזה ובזה. כך מפרש בגמרא: דבבני יונה פסולין משום גודלן, ובתורין מפני קוטנן, דיצאו מכלל קטנים ולכלל גדולים לא באו:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:13:2.english: The correct reading in the mishna is: "The beginning of the yellowing, in this one and in that one, is disqualified" - The beginning of the yellowing, when they begin to grow a fine yellow feather around the neck, [the birds] are disqualified, both in this [type] and in that. So it is explained in the Gemara: that young pigeons are disqualified because of their size [being too large], and turtledoves because of their smallness, as they have left the category of small ones but have not yet entered the category of large ones.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:15:1.english: Large turtledoves and not small - [The phrase "large and not small"] refers to the "turtledoves" (torim) of the verse.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:15:2.hebrew: גדולים ולא קטנים - לקמיה מפרש מאי משמע:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:15:2.english: Adults and not young ones - Later [the Gemara] explains what indicates this:

Rashi on Chullin 22a:15:3.hebrew: שיכול והלא דין הוא - אי לאו דכתיב תורים, הוה ילפינן מדינא דקטנים כשרים:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:15:3.english: For one might think: and is it not a logical inference? - Had it not been written "turtledoves," we would have derived by logical inference that the young ones are valid.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:1:1.hebrew: אוחז בראש ובגוף ומזה - לאחר מליקה הויא הזאה, כדכתיב בחטאת העוף גבי שמיעת קול (ויקרא ה): והזה מדם החטאת וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 22a:1:1.english: He holds the head and the body, and sprinkles - After the pinching [melika] comes the sprinkling, as it is written regarding the sin-offering of a bird, in the case of hearing a voice (Leviticus 5): "And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin-offering," etc.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:2:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - דהא "אוחז בראש ובגוף" משמע שצריך לאוחזן שניהן בתוך כף ידו, ולא סגי ליה לאחוז בראש או בגוף. ומנא ליה הא בחטאת:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:2:1.english: What is he saying? - For [the phrase] "he holds the head and the body" implies that he must hold both of them in the palm of his hand, and it does not suffice for him to hold only the head or only the body. And from where does he derive this [requirement] in the case of a sin-offering?

Rashi on Chullin 22a:2:2.hebrew: כשהוא אחוז הראש בגוף - שמחובר הראש בגוף בשעת הזאה, דהא כתיב "ולא יבדיל":
Rashi on Chullin 22a:2:2.english: When the head is attached to the body - That the head is connected to the body at the time of the sprinkling, as it is written (Vayikra 5:8), "and he shall not divide [it]."

Rashi on Chullin 22a:2:3.hebrew: אף כאן כו' - דע"כ היקישא להכי אתא, דהא מול עורף מג"ש נפקא ליה לקמן, וכמשפט חטאת בהמה לא אמרינן, דהא מעוף סליק:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:2:3.english: Here too, etc. - Necessarily, the analogy ["as the law of a sin-offering of an animal"] came for this purpose [to teach that the pinching is done at the nape], for [the requirement of] pinching at the nape is derived for it later from a *gezera shava*, and we do not say "like the law of an animal sin-offering" [to apply other laws of that offering], since [the verse] speaks of a bird ("ascends from a bird").

Rashi on Chullin 22a:3:1.english: "And he shall offer it" - [This teaches] that it requires a partial separation [of the head from the body].

Rashi on Chullin 22a:4:1.hebrew: והקריבו למה לי - לחלק, דלא נימא כמשפט חטאת העוף בסימן אחד, דהא אתקש מליקה להקטרה:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:4:1.english: And "he shall bring it near" (vehikrivo) – why do I need it? - To distinguish [between the bird sin-offering and the animal sin-offering], so that we would not say that [the verse's phrase] "according to the ordinance" means that the bird sin-offering [requires] one sign [to be cut], since melikah (pinching the neck) was compared to haktarah (burning on the altar).

Rashi on Chullin 22a:5:1.english: Behold, "like the law of the sin-offering of a bird" - [This refers to the law] which he had finished with [i.e., the sin-offering of a bird, which the Gemara had just discussed].

Rashi on Chullin 22a:6:1.hebrew: ואי משום ומלק והקטיר - ההוא הוה מפקינן ליה לדרשא אחרינא, דמיניה נפקא לן מליקת עולת העוף דלמעלה מחוט הסיקרא היא, בראש המזבח, דאילו מליקת חטאת העוף למטה, כדילפינן לה בזבחים (דף סד:) "על קיר המזבח" זה קיר התחתון כו' בפרק קדשי קדשים. וכיון דמיבעי לן למילתא אחריתא, לא אלים למעקר היקישא דכמשפט מההוא דסליק מיניה, דאיכא למדרש היקישא דמליקה והקטרה לענין ראש המזבח, והיקישא דכמשפט לענין אחיזת ראש וגוף:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:6:1.english: And if [the reason were] because of "and he shall wring its neck and burn it" - That [verse] we would take out for a different derivation, for from it we derive that the wringing of a bird burnt-offering is done above the red line [of the altar], at the top of the altar, whereas the wringing of a bird sin-offering is below, as we derive it in Zevachim (page 64b): "On the wall of the altar" - this is the lower wall, etc., in the chapter "Kodshei Kodashim." And since we need it for that other matter, it is not strong enough to uproot the comparison of "according to the ordinance" from that [verse] from which it was removed [as a source for this law], for it is possible to expound the comparison of wringing and burning as relating to the top of the altar, and the comparison of "according to the ordinance" as relating to holding the head and the body.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:7:1.hebrew: השתא דכתיב והקריבו - על כרחך עקריה מיניה דחילוק לגמרי משמע ליה לתנא קמא, דלא תיגמר מיניה כלל, ואוקמיה אחטאת בהמה. ומהשתא דריש מומלק והקטיר, דלגמרי איתקש הקטרה למליקה, בין לענין ראשו של מזבח, בין לענין הראש בעצמו והגוף בעצמו:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:7:1.english: Now that it is written "and he shall bring it near" - You are forced to say that [the verse] uproots [the halakha] from [the case of a bird sin-offering], since the first Tanna understands it as a complete distinction, so that nothing should be derived from it at all, and he establishes it as referring to an animal sin-offering. And from now on he expounds "and he shall wring its neck... and he shall burn it" [as meaning] that burning is entirely equated with wringing, both with regard to the top of the altar, and with regard to the head by itself and the body by itself.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:8:1.hebrew: משלו ולא משל ציבור - מתרומת הלשכה:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:8:1.english: From his own, and not from the public's - From the [funds of the] Temple chamber's collection.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:8:2.hebrew: משלו ולא משל מעשר - דתרי "אשר לו" כתובים בפרשה, ואפילו לרבי יהודה דאמר מעשר ממון הדיוט הוא, להכי אתא "אשר לו" לממעטיה. "וביום" ו"בידו הימנית" נמי בפר יום הכפורים כתיב: "כי ביום הזה יכפר", וכתיב ביה אצבע וכהונה: "והזה באצבעו אל פני" וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 22a:8:2.english: From his own, and not from the tithe - For "which is his" is written twice in the passage, and even according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says that the tithe is ordinary property, "which is his" comes for this purpose, to exclude it. And "on the day" and "with his right hand" are also [derived] from the bull of Yom Kippur, for it is written: "For on this day he shall atone," and written there are "finger" and priesthood: "And he shall sprinkle with his finger on the face of" etc.

Rashi on Chullin 22a:9:1.hebrew: מביום צוותו נפקא - למה ליה למילפא מחטאת בהמה? הא בכולהו קרבנות כתיב "ביום צוותו להקריב", דמשמע ביום ולא בלילה, וכל הקרבנות במשמע:
Rashi on Chullin 22a:9:1.english: Isn't it derived from "on the day He commanded"? - Why does [the Gemara] need to derive it from the sin-offering of an animal? Regarding all the sacrifices it is written, "on the day He commanded [the children of Israel] to offer" (Leviticus 7:38), which implies by day and not at night, and this includes all the sacrifices.

Tosafot on Chullin 22a:11:1.hebrew: ואידך כהונה בעי אצבע - בסוף התודה (מנחות פג.) משני "ידו הימנית כדי נסבה"; ובסוף דם חטאת (זבחים דף צח.) משני "תרווייהו כי הכא". ונראה דלמ"ד דבר הלמד בג"ש אינו חוזר ומלמד בהיקש, צ"ל דכדי נסבה דאצבע; חטאת גופיה יליף בגזרה שוה ממצורע, דהיינו ימין, בפ"ק דזבחים (דף יג) ובפ"ק דמנחות (דף י.). ואם כן, היכי מצי למילף עולת העוף מחטאת מהיקישא דכמשפט:
Tosafot on Chullin 22a:11:1.english: And the other [Tanna holds that] priesthood requires a finger - At the end of [the passage on] the thanksgiving offering (Menachot 83a), [the Gemara] answers: "his right hand" was stated merely incidentally (kedei nasva). And at the end of [the passage on] the blood of the sin-offering (Zevachim 98a), [the Gemara] answers: "both of them, as here." And it appears that according to the one who holds that a matter learned through a verbal analogy (gezerah shavah) does not return and teach through a comparison (heikesh), one must say that [the mention of] "finger" is incidental; the sin-offering itself is derived by a verbal analogy from the leper, namely [that the right hand is required], in the first chapter of Zevachim (13a) and in the first chapter of Menachot (10a). And if so, how can [the Gemara] derive the bird burnt-offering from the sin-offering through the comparison of "according to the ordinance" (ke-mishpat)?

Tosafot on Chullin 22a:14:1.hebrew: נמצא כשר בתורין כו' - אברייתא דהכא לא שייך למידק האי "נמצא", למעוטי מאי, כדדייק לעיל אמתניתין דנמצא כשר בשחיטה פסול במליקה. דהך ברייתא אמתניתין קיימא לפרושי דתורין גדולים כשרים כו', והדר מסיים "נמצא" כמו שאמרה משנתינו. אבל לעיל לא צריך למתני כלל "נמצא", דכבר אשמועינן רישא דשחיטה מן הצואר ומליקה מן העורף, ואם שינה בזה ובזה פסול:
Tosafot on Chullin 22a:14:1.english: "It is found that it is valid with turtledoves," etc. - On the baraita here, it is not relevant to infer from this word "it is found" [in order] to exclude something, as [the Gemara] inferred above regarding the Mishnah, [from the words] "it is found that it is valid with slaughter [but] invalid with pinching (melikah)." For this baraita stands to explain the Mishnah, [teaching] that large turtledoves are valid, etc., and it then concludes "it is found," as our Mishnah stated. But above, it was not necessary at all to teach "it is found," since the first clause already taught us that slaughter is from the neck and pinching is from the nape, and if one switched between them, [the offering] is invalid:

Tosafot on Chullin 22a:15:1.hebrew: שיכול והלא דין הוא - בשום דוכתא ל"ג תרווייהו, דשיכול משמע דאי לאו האי קרא לא הוה אמינא הכי; אבל והלא דין הוא משמע דבלאו האי קרא היה לו לומר כן:
Tosafot on Chullin 22a:15:1.english: For I might have thought; and is it not logical? - Nowhere is the text [of the Gemara] to have both of them, for "I might have thought" (she-yakhol) implies that were it not for this verse I would not have said so; but "and is it not logical?" implies that even without this verse, one should have said so.

Tosafot on Chullin 22a:15:2.hebrew: שיכול ומה בני יונה כו' - פירוש, אי לאו קרא דתורים הייתי מכשיר אפילו קטנים מקל וחומר. ואם תאמר, ואי לא כתיב קרא דתורים לא הוה ידעינן תורין כלל דכשרים לקרבן? ויש לומר דהכי פירושו: שיכול, אי לאו דאקיש רחמנא תורים לבני יונה דמינה ילפינן בסמוך דתורין קטנים לא, אלא היה כתוב תורים רחוק מבני יונה, דהשתא היה משמע תורים בין גדולים בין קטנים, ואפילו בלא קל וחומר הוה ידעינן, אלא דניחא ליה למנקט למילף בקל וחומר. אי נמי, דהוה מצי למכתב בני יונה ותורים, דהשתא לא הוה מקיש תורים לבני יונה, דאיכא למימר דקאי נמי בני אתורים, ומכל מקום גדולים כשרים מדלא כתוב בהדיא בני יונה ובני תורים, והוה אמינא מקל וחומר דכולם כשרים. ת"ל תורים, דמשמע גדולים דוקא, כדמפרש לקמן, דומיא דבני יונה:
Tosafot on Chullin 22a:15:2.english: For one might [have thought]: If young doves, etc. - The explanation is: Were it not for the verse of "turtledoves" (torim), I would have deemed even the small ones valid by a kal va-chomer. And if you say: If the verse of "turtledoves" were not written, we would not know at all that turtledoves are valid for an offering? One can answer that this is its explanation: For one might [have thought] — were it not that the Merciful One juxtaposed turtledoves to young doves (bnei yonah), from which we derive below that small turtledoves are not [valid] — but rather "turtledoves" had been written distant from "young doves," for then it would have implied turtledoves, whether large or small, and even without a kal va-chomer we would have known [that they are valid], except that it is preferable for him to derive it by a kal va-chomer. Alternatively, [the Torah] could have written "young doves and turtledoves," so that it would not have juxtaposed turtledoves to young doves, since one could say that "young" (bnei) also refers to the turtledoves; and in any case, large ones are valid, since it was not explicitly written "young doves and young turtledoves," and I would have said by a kal va-chomer that all of them are valid. Therefore the verse states "turtledoves," which implies specifically large ones, as [the Gemara] explains below, similar to young doves.
